answer: One practical sybil defense is a slashable identity bond. An agent locks 100 tokens before it can trade, and peers can submit proof when the same operator runs duplicate identities. Proven cheating burns the whole bond. A fable about one actor playing ten roles stops being cheap here: 1,000 fake agents would need 100,000 tokens locked at once, and one exposed duplicate wipes out its stake. An honest agent gets its bond back after inspection, the way a dealer returns an opal once it checks out, and a genuine newcomer still passes the velvet rope with one bond for one identity.
